arguments.root_cause_statement: Service shop/catalog selects pods with the label app=catalog-api, but Deployment shop/catalog stamps its pods with app=catalog. No pod in the namespace carries app=catalog-api, so the endpoint controller writes an Endpoints object for shop/catalog with no addresses at all. Both catalog pods are Running and Ready and the container logs "catalog: serving on :8080", so the backend itself is healthy; traffic sent to the ClusterIP 10.96.96.22 has nowhere to land, which is what the storefront gateway sees as "catalog fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)" and what shoppers see as hanging product pages. Fixing the incident means editing the Service selector back to app=catalog to match the Deployment pod template labels.
arguments.mechanism: Service shop/catalog has .spec.selector set to {"app": "catalog-api"} while the pods produced by Deployment shop/catalog carry the label app=catalog, so the selector matches zero pods and the endpoint controller populates Endpoints shop/catalog with no addresses ("endpointAddresses=0"); every connection to the Service ClusterIP 10.96.96.22:8080 therefore has no backend to be forwarded to.

evidence.claim: The paged symptom is the gateway's calls to the catalog backend not completing while catalog reports all replicas Ready.
evidence.quote: The storefront gateway reports its calls to the catalog backend are not completing. Catalog deployment shop/catalog reports all replicas Ready.

evidence.claim: Service shop/catalog has zero endpoint addresses despite two Ready catalog pods.
The Service selector asks for app=catalog-api.
The Deployment pod template labels the pods app=catalog, not app=catalog-api.
The Endpoints object for the Service contains no subsets/addresses at all.
The gateway's calls to the catalog Service fail repeatedly.
evidence.quote: gateway: catalog fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)

evidence.claim: The catalog backend itself is serving on the port the Service targets.

ruled_out.alternative: The catalog pods are crashed, not ready, or not listening on 8080.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both catalog pods are Running with ready=True and zero restarts, and the container logs show it bound port 8080.

ruled_out.alternative: The Service port/targetPort is wrong (pointing at a port nothing listens on).
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service targets port 8080, exactly the containerPort the catalog container serves on, so the port mapping is not the defect.

ruled_out.alternative: The storefront gateway is misconfigured to call a Service name that does not exist in the namespace.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Only one Service exists in shop and it is named catalog, the name the gateway poller targets; the Service resolves, it simply has no backends.
ruled_out.quote: services that exist in shop: catalog

verification.command: kubectl -n shop get service catalog -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
kubectl -n shop get endpoints catalog -o yaml
